summary.text: Titan son of Uranus and Gaia, joined with the sea-goddess Eurybia and father of Astraeus, Pallas and Perses, a branch leading to the winds, stars, Hecate and the divine powers of victory and force.

story.text: Hesiod numbers Crius among the sons Gaia bore after lying with starry Uranus, between Coeus and Hyperion in the roll of the Titans. Pseudo-Apollodorus repeats his place among the male children of Earth and Sky.

Bright Eurybia, daughter of Pontus, was joined in love with Crius and bore three sons: great Astraeus, Pallas and Perses, whom Hesiod calls eminent in wisdom. Through Astraeus and Dawn came the strong-hearted winds and the stars; Perses fathered Hecate by Asteria, while Pallas fathered Victory, Dominion, Emulation and Violence by Styx.
